biography: Kimi Kim's journey began not on a racetrack, but amidst the neon-drenched arcades of Osaka. The rhythmic hum of racing simulators, the simulated roar of engines, became his sanctuary. By age 12, he was consistently topping local arcade leaderboards, a feat that caught the attention of a retired karting instructor, Mr. Sato. Sato, seeing raw talent, took Kimi under his wing. Lacking significant family wealth, Kimi and Sato rebuilt discarded karts, scavenging parts and burning the midnight oil in a small garage. His initial regional karting success led to a scholarship with a small independent team, where he quickly rose through the ranks. Despite lacking the backing of major sponsors, Kimi's consistent podium finishes and unwavering focus have made him a rising star in the junior racing scene, proving that passion and dedication can overcome financial limitations.
drivingStyle: Kimi's driving style is characterized by a calculated smoothness. He is not one for flamboyant overtakes or risky maneuvers. Instead, he focuses on maximizing corner entry speed and maintaining momentum. Tire management is his forte; he can consistently extract the most performance from his tires over a race distance. Under pressure, Kimi remains remarkably composed, rarely making mistakes even when challenged by faster opponents.

rivalries.reason: A childhood friend turned fierce competitor in karting, Ren always had the advantage of superior equipment, fueling a competitive fire within Kimi.
Ayumi, a well-funded driver with a reputation for aggressive driving, constantly tries to intimidate Kimi on the track, leading to several close calls and a simmering rivalry.
Hiroshi, a veteran driver in the junior formula, sees Kimi as a threat to his established position and frequently uses his experience to outmaneuver him, creating friction both on and off the track.

quirks: Always polishes his helmet visor three times before entering the car.
Listens to traditional Japanese flute music on noise-canceling headphones before each race.
Carries a small, worn origami crane his grandfather made him for good luck.
careerHighlight: Winning the Junior Formula Regional Championship in his rookie season against all odds, securing the title at the final race with a perfectly executed overtake on the last lap.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in a crucial race due to a mechanical failure, costing him valuable championship points and shaking his confidence.
